title: Alter Your Perspective
coreMove: Change the angle of view until a truthful opening appears inside facts that first looked closed.
sourcePressure: This chapter belongs to Perception, so it must teach cleaner seeing before it teaches action or endurance. Source sidecar ch05 exists and provides partial-source support only; no full text is frozen. For "Alter Your Perspective", the pressure is to teach this exact move: Change the angle of view until a truthful opening appears inside facts that first looked closed.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version turns the chapter into generic mindset advice instead of a precise discipline of reading the obstacle cleanly. For "Alter Your Perspective", avoid replacing the chapter move with the whole book thesis.

sourceAnchors.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
sourceAnchors.detail: Frozen notes connect Eisenhower to seeing opportunity where others see disaster, without supporting a detailed wartime retelling.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Eisenhower should enter as a restrained example of a mind looking for usable room inside what others called disaster.

hook: A generic obstacle appears and teaches alter your perspective
The problem is not the problem
Everything changed when the setback arrived
counterintuition: The obstacle is actually a blessing
The hard part is really your mindset
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on adversity
Write down three things you are grateful for
Take a breath and choose courage
examples: generic office meeting with laptop and coffee
